note: relocs() assigns the newly created RList to obj->relocs_list and returns the same list pointer to the caller.
r_bin_object_set_items() calls relocs(bf) which returns the list that was also stored in obj->relocs_list.
The caller frees the returned list after setting l->free=NULL, but obj->relocs_list still points to the freed memory, creating a dangling pointer.

The caller sets obj->relocs_list to NULL after freeing, but this only happens in the caller's local scope; the RBinBfltObj's relocs_list field was already overwritten by relocs() and is not reset here.
When r_bin_bflt_free() is called during r_bin_file_free(), it calls r_list_free() on the dangling relocs_list pointer, causing a heap-use-after-free.
r_bin_file_free() invokes the plugin destroy callback which calls r_bin_bflt_free(), triggering the UAF on the stale relocs_list pointer.
